finding.claim: authorize() is async but not awaited in DELETE /reports/:id. The deletion runs without waiting for the check, so any authenticated user can delete any report. The rejected promise is never handled, so it is an unhandled rejection that on Node 15+ can crash the process (DoS).
finding.source: Authenticated user (any session) sending DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary report id

trace.note: authorize(...) called without await, result ignored. The 403 throw becomes a rejected promise that nothing handles.
remove executes immediately, regardless of the authorization outcome

finding.guards_checked: authorize() would enforce grants, but its Promise is not awaited, so the handler never sees the throw. No other middleware performs authorization (the only app.use sets req.user). The PUT route awaits correctly, which confirms the DELETE omission is a bug.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws 403 on missing grant, but the DELETE handler calls it without await at line 20, so nothing waits for or catches the rejection. The only middleware (server.js:4-7) sets req.user and does no authorization.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls the async authorize() as a bare statement, so db.reports.remove at server.js:21 runs regardless of the check. The rejected promise is also unhandled, which on Node 15+ can crash the process. The PUT route awaits it correctly at server.js:27.

finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /reports/:id passes the whole request body to db.reports.update. A caller with only 'write' grant on the report can set arbitrary fields such as owner_id, tenant_id or id, which can reassign ownership or change protected attributes.

trace.note: unfiltered body is applied to the record

finding.guards_checked: No field allowlist or schema validation on the path. authorize() checks only the action grant, not which fields may change. The db implementation is not in the repo, so the exact fields that can be set are unconfirmed.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 is awaited at line 27 and throws a 403 on a missing 'write' grant. It checks only the action, not which fields may change. There is no field allowlist or schema validation, and express.json() at line 3 only parses the body.
verdict.reason: server.js:28 passes the unfiltered req.body to db.reports.update after only a 'write' grant check (server.js:27). Any authenticated user with write access can therefore submit protected fields such as owner_id. db is not defined in the repo, so I could not confirm which fields it actually accepts.
